intro.text: A smooth, slide-based presentation comparing the two countries. It charts shared seafaring history, culinary crossovers and language links, and also covers family, faith, dress, crafts, architecture, music, celebrations and people.

ui.hint: Swipe, scroll or use the arrow keys

slides.title: The Art of Welcome
slides.text: Hospitality is a way of life. In Tunisia a guest is greeted with Marhba and offered tea with pine nuts, and jasmine posies are given as a sign of welcome. In Bahrain a guest is greeted with Ahlan wa sahlan and served Arabic coffee from the dallah with dates. In both countries refusing a second cup is a polite gesture, and a guest is never allowed to leave hungry.
